key_insight: UniG2U-Bench provides the first systematic framework to evaluate when and how generative capabilities of unified multimodal models translate into improved visual understanding, by organizing generation-to-understanding (G2U) evaluation into concrete regimes and subtasks.
problem_solved: Existing benchmarks do not systematically identify which understanding tasks benefit from generative reasoning or what kinds of visual transformations (implicit vs. explicit) drive gains; UniG2U-Bench fills that gap with a structured, testable taxonomy.
method: Design a comprehensive benchmark that decomposes G2U evaluation into 7 regimes and 30 subtasks reflecting different degrees of implicit or explicit visual transformation.
Provide task definitions, evaluation protocols, and representative examples to probe whether generative abilities lead to better understanding across those regimes.
Apply the benchmark to unified multimodal models to reveal patterns in when generation assists understanding (enabling comparative analysis and model diagnosis).
impact: Helps researchers and engineers diagnose when to leverage unified generative models for downstream visual understanding tasks, guiding model selection, architecture design, and targeted improvements in multimodal systems.
visual_elements: Flow diagram showing the G2U evaluation pipeline: input image → generation step (implicit/explicit) → understanding task → metrics
Grid/heatmap mapping 7 regimes × 30 subtasks with color-coded performance or difficulty
Before/after visual transformation examples illustrating implicit vs. explicit transformations
Bar/line chart comparing model performance across regimes to highlight where generation helps most
paper_title: UniG2U-Bench: Do Unified Models Advance Multimodal Understanding?
paper_authors: Zimo Wen, Boxiu Li, Wanbo Zhang, Junxiang Lei, Xiaoyu Chen
